subject: botany_2
question_text: Write a brief note on chromosomal mutations and gene mutations.

insider_note: Scale is the whole answer: a chromosome versus a single base pair. Say that in one line and both halves fall into place.

page_header: Principles of Inheritance and Variation (Botany-II) · 4 marks

steps.label: What a mutation is
steps.margin_note: Definition plus the two kinds named. Four lines.
lines: A MUTATION is a sudden, heritable change in the
genetic material of an organism.
Mutations are of two main kinds:
1. chromosomal mutations  2. gene mutations
steps.why: Both kinds are changes to the same DNA and differ only in how much of it changes, which is why they belong under one definition.
common_mistakes: Saying mutations are always harmful. Many are neutral and some are useful.
Saying mutations are not inherited. A mutation in a germ cell IS inherited.
steps.memory_tip: Sudden, heritable, and of two sizes.

steps.label: Chromosomal mutation
steps.margin_note: Both kinds of change, the term aberration, and one example.
lines: 1. CHROMOSOMAL MUTATION is a change in the
NUMBER or the STRUCTURE of chromosomes.
Loss or gain of a segment of DNA alters the
chromosome.
Such changes are called chromosomal
ABERRATIONS.
Example: they are commonly seen in CANCER
cells.
steps.why: A chromosome carries hundreds of genes, so changing one affects many genes at once — which is why the effects are usually severe.
common_mistakes: Saying a chromosomal mutation changes one base. That is a GENE mutation.
Giving only structure. NUMBER changes are chromosomal mutations too.
steps.memory_tip: Whole chromosomes: their number or their shape.

steps.label: Gene mutation
steps.margin_note: Definition, the other name, and the named disease.
lines: 2. GENE MUTATION is a change in a SINGLE
BASE PAIR of DNA.
It is also called a POINT MUTATION.
Example: SICKLE CELL ANAEMIA in humans,
caused by a single base change in the gene for the
beta chain of haemoglobin.
steps.why: One base changed means one amino acid changed, and sickle cell anaemia shows that a single such change can be enough to cause a disease.
common_mistakes: Saying a gene mutation affects the whole chromosome. It affects ONE base pair.
Naming no example. Sickle cell anaemia is the standard one.
steps.memory_tip: One base pair, one amino acid, one disease.

steps.label: The difference
steps.margin_note: One line naming scale as the difference. Five lines.

lines.text: Chromosomal: many genes. Gene: one base pair

lines: A chromosomal mutation changes many genes at
once, because a chromosome carries many genes.
A gene mutation changes one base pair in one
gene.
The difference between them is one of SCALE.
steps.why: Naming the difference as one of scale is the shortest correct summary and shows the two were not simply memorised as separate facts.
common_mistakes: Treating the two as unrelated. Both are changes to DNA; only the amount differs.
Ending without a comparison. The question sets them side by side, so compare them.
steps.memory_tip: Same material, different amount of it.
